Does DeepSeek Harness even support setting a host? As far as I know, it's designed almost completely for localhost usage, which may be why it has all the localhost checking.

For `.dsh/storages`: does DSH store only caches in the storages folder, or does it store other useful data? We need to make sure. If it's only cache, then we don't need to sync it; if it stores other useful things, then we may need to sync it.

`.devvm-id` makes sense. The project path was actually standardized to `/workspace`, but DSH defaults to the root or home directory when you select a workspace. For ergonomics, perhaps link it to `/root/workspace` instead. The workspace path is part of the session log, so `/root/workspace` would be stable.

For real-time sync, are you suggesting we write our own utility that monitors filesystem activity on close-write? That seems overcomplicated. DSH saves sessions as append-only JSON Lines. I feel like monitoring it from outside is working around it. Does DSH expose a seam for the session writer or session persistence? Could we replace the writing backend while keeping the same behavior and save to a database? If it exposes an acceptable contract, reads and writes could all be handled there. Then we wouldn't need to worry about single-writer semantics in the same way; if it's an SQL database, the database handles locking and related behavior.

For the beginning, we can assume one user and that a chat will not be written simultaneously.
